answer: An agent economy can price each fake identity at one fresh, graded essay per epoch: every account gets a private prompt, and a similarity scan compares all answers before payout. Like water cutting channels through karst, reused reasoning leaves a traceable path, so two accounts that rephrase one draft, the way a sonnet keeps its rhymes, are both zeroed. A farm of 100 heads must buy 100 truly distinct essays every 6 hours, which can't be bulk-copied. The scan acts as a lantern for graders; its limit is that skilled paraphrase still slips through sometimes.
